Routines for Lighting Levels

Purpose: keep the Companion Animal Travel Desk calm, clear, and ready so every animal and traveler gets steady support from booking through pickup.

We keep the desk area softly lit during normal handling and raise the light only when the work calls for sharper visibility. The shift lead checks that lamps do not shine straight into a carrier, because pets settle better when the space feels even and quiet. If a traveler arrives nervous, we lower glare where we can, speak in a calm voice, and keep movement around the counter simple. Crew members should also watch for shadows that may spook an animal during handoff, since a smooth handoff matters as much as the paperwork.

When a pet needs a relief stop, we guide the traveler with clear directions and confirm the route before they leave the desk. <<FACT F014>> We do not crowd the pet area, and we keep our tone light so the traveler can focus on the pet rather than the pressure of the airport.

If an animal is marked for extra watchfulness, the desk stays close to the coordinating teams and keeps the area tidy. <<FACT F030>> We use plain instructions, check carrier latches, and make sure water, bedding, and documents are easy to reach. If the traveler asks for help, we answer without rushing and we keep the process steady from one step to the next.

For lounge handoffs, the desk shares only the needed details and lets the receiving team manage the space once the pet is settled. <<FACT F001>> We then note the change in the station log, check that the traveler has the next point of contact, and return the desk to a calm state for the next arrival.

If anything feels off, tell the shift coordinator right away so we can sort it out with the service team.
